correctness.rationale: The state triple stores the final symbol, newest dinucleotide and exactly those older dinucleotides disjoint from a next appended pair; an induction proves the transition rule accepts the full two-stem avoidance language. Exhaustive BFS explores all 22,985 reachable good states and the sink. Moore partitions stabilize after suffix length five at 7,311 classes and give a right congruence; a separate Hopcroft minimization also returns 7,311. Direct index-pair evaluation agreed on all 349,525 words through length nine. The finite graph traversal, not finite-word extrapolation, proves the all-length bound.

originality.rationale: The exact one-pass deterministic state count 7,311 and five-nucleotide distinguishing-suffix bound concern the full disjoint reverse-complement dinucleotide-avoidance language. The primary literature formulates this avoidance and analyzes code constructions and asymptotic capacity, but the inspected claims and methods do not give the exact minimal DFA for the full language; their small de Bruijn graphs describe restricted generating families. Direct searches and relevant repository comparisons revealed no equal or stronger state-count theorem. Historical priority is qualified by possible unindexed older work.

value.rationale: The minimal complete DFA size is a natural, uniquely determined finite-memory complexity of exact DNA secondary-structure avoidance at the smallest modeled stem length. The result sharpens online checking from an unminimized 22,986-state recognizer to an optimal 7,311-state device and fixes the necessary/sufficient 13 binary state bits. It is not merely an arbitrary slice or known capacity recomputation: the prior six-vertex coding subgraphs do not recognize the entire language. It also exposes a five-nucleotide distinguishing-suffix horizon usable in minimization or finite-length enumerative methods. No general-stem or rate improvement is claimed.
